newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ coalition govt's popularity slumps in poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ coalition govt's popularity slumps in poll.

text.p: The New Zealand centre-right coalition government's approval rating slumped to just 13 percent with 78 percent disapproving its performance, according to a TV1 poll published on Tuesday.
The disapproval rating in the last poll on May 12 was at 75 percent.
The centre-left opposition Labour Party remained the most popular party with 41 percent, down one point.
The centre-right National Party gained one point to 38 percent. It's nationalist New Zealand First partner was down one on four percent.
The left-wing Alliance Party was up one to seven percentand the radical free-market ACT Party was steady on five percent.
Translated into seats, Labour would have 51, National 49, the Alliance eight, ACT six and NZ First six, meaning the coalition would still have a majority if it received support from ACT.
Labour leader Helen Clark jumped five percent as the most preferred prime minister, to 26 percent.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger of the National Party gained a point to 21 percent and NZ First leader Winston Peters was steady on four percent along with National Party senior minister Jenny Shipley.
The poll was of 1,000 people and comes just ahead of Thursday's budget to be delivered by Treasurer Peters.
